html:
The French zone was the part of defeated Germany that France occupied from 1945 to 1949, in the southwest: the left bank of the Rhine around the Palatinate, southern Baden and southern Württemberg.

France had not been given a zone at first. At the Yalta conference Britain argued for one, and it was carved out of land meant for the British and Americans. De Gaulle's government wanted security above all: a weak Germany, reparations and control of coal. France took factories and timber, and in 1947 split off the Saarland as a separate Saar Protectorate tied to the French economy.

French policy softened as the Cold War grew. France joined its zone to the British and American ones in 1949, and it became part of West Germany, within Allied-occupied Germany as a whole. The Saar returned to Germany in 1957.
sum: The French zone was the part of defeated Germany that France occupied from 1945 to 1949, in the southwest: the left bank of the Rhine around the Palatinate, southern Baden and southern Württemberg.
